input.strategy_title: FIPS 140-3 compliance for the model serving stack
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Public-sector deals require the model serving stack to run on FIPS-enabled
OpenShift clusters using validated cryptographic modules. Today KServe
components and the serving data plane link non-validated crypto libraries in
several images, and we have no compliance evidence package. Certification
involves an external accredited laboratory (historical turnaround: six to nine
months) and mandatory security review board sign-off at defined milestones —
these human and third-party gates dominate the schedule regardless of
engineering speed.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | All serving-stack images run correctly on FIPS-enabled clusters using validated crypto modules (no non-validated crypto in the request path). |
| HLR-2 | P0 | A compliance evidence package (module inventory, build attestations, test results) is assembled and submitted through the security review board to the external certification lab. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | CI enforces FIPS regressions: a gating check fails any serving-stack build that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation states the FIPS support posture and cluster prerequisites. |

## Affected Components

- KServe
- Platform Operator

## Out of Scope

- FIPS posture for workbenches, pipelines, and training (separate strategies)
- Common Criteria certification

## Open Questions

None on scope — but note that lab scheduling and review-board cadence are
externally controlled and cannot be compressed by engineering effort.

# FIPS 140-3 crypto module remediation for KServe serving-stack images

## Description

This epic delivers FIPS 140-3 compliance for the KServe portion of the model
serving stack. Every container image shipped by the KServe component is audited
for non-validated cryptographic library usage, remediated to use validated
crypto modules, and verified to run correctly on FIPS-enabled OpenShift
clusters. The epic also carries the KServe-side CI regression gate so
non-validated crypto usage cannot be reintroduced by future builds.

## Scope

- Audit all container images shipped by the KServe component (including the
  serving data plane images it deploys that belong to this component) and
  document every linkage to non-validated cryptographic libraries, with
  particular attention to the request path.
- Remediate each identified image so that no non-validated crypto is used in
  the request path, replacing it with validated cryptographic modules.
- Rebuild the remediated images through the component's existing build
  pipeline so that build attestations are produced for the compliant images.
- Verify that the remediated images serve inference requests correctly on a
  FIPS-enabled OpenShift cluster, and collect the verification results.
- Add a gating CI check that fails any KServe serving-stack build that
  reintroduces non-validated crypto usage, wired into CI for those builds.
- Confirm no functional regression on non-FIPS clusters.
- Hand off the KServe module inventory, build attestations, and verification
  results for inclusion in the compliance evidence package.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A documented audit covers every KServe serving-stack image and identifies
   all non-validated crypto library linkages (pass/fail: the inventory exists
   and covers every image in scope).
2. Every image identified by the audit is remediated so that no non-validated
   crypto is used in the request path (pass/fail per image).
3. The remediated images build successfully in the component's existing build
   pipeline and produce build attestations.
4. Verification results demonstrate that inference serving works correctly on
   a FIPS-enabled OpenShift cluster with the remediated images.
5. A gating CI check fails any KServe serving-stack build that reintroduces
   non-validated crypto usage, and the check is wired into CI for those
   builds (pass/fail: a deliberately non-compliant build fails the gate).
6. The remediated images show no functional regression on non-FIPS clusters.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)** — KServe share: all KServe serving-stack images run correctly
  on FIPS-enabled clusters using validated crypto modules, with no
  non-validated crypto in the request path.
- **HLR-3 (P1, bundled)** — KServe share of the FIPS regression CI enforcement:
  the gating check for KServe builds is carried in this epic because it guards
  the same image builds this epic remediates (shared surface; not separately
  schedulable from the remediation it guards).

## Risks / Notes

- Verification on a FIPS-enabled OpenShift cluster requires access to such a
  cluster; the acceptance criteria sit on the verification deliverables, and
  cluster access is an environment prerequisite to be secured during
  execution.
- The exact set of affected images and libraries is unknown until the audit
  runs; the remediation covers whatever the audit finds (fix-and-retry), which
  is why no separate investigation epic is needed.

- Remediate each identified image so that no non-validated crypto is used in

- Verify that the remediated operator deploys and manages the serving stack
  correctly on a FIPS-enabled OpenShift cluster, and collect the verification

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A documented audit covers every Platform Operator image and identifies all
   non-validated crypto library linkages (pass/fail: the inventory exists and

   non-validated crypto usage, and the check is wired into CI for those

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)** — Platform Operator share: all Platform Operator images run

# FIPS 140-3 compliance evidence package and certification submission

## Description

This epic assembles the FIPS 140-3 compliance evidence package for the model
serving stack — module inventory, build attestations, and test results — and
drives it through the mandatory security review board milestones to submission
at the external accredited certification laboratory. It is the strategy's
compliance-delivery epic: its engineering deliverable ends at a complete,
reviewed, and submitted evidence package.

## Scope

- Assemble the module inventory covering every serving-stack image (KServe and
  Platform Operator), consolidated from the component-level audits.
- Collect the build attestations produced by the serving-stack components'
  build pipelines for the remediated images.
- Collect the FIPS verification test results demonstrating correct operation
  of the remediated images on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters.
- Structure and package the evidence according to the certification
  requirements communicated by the security review board and the certification
  lab.
- Deliver the evidence required at each defined security review board
  milestone and present it for sign-off.
- Submit the final package to the external accredited certification lab and
  track the submission status.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The evidence package contains a complete module inventory covering every
   serving-stack image (KServe and Platform Operator).
2. The evidence package includes the build attestations produced by the
   serving-stack components' build pipelines for the remediated images.
3. The evidence package includes the test results demonstrating correct
   operation of the remediated images on FIPS-enabled clusters.
4. The evidence required at each defined security review board milestone is
   delivered and presented (pass/fail per milestone).
5. The final evidence package is submitted to the external certification lab
   (pass/fail: the submission is complete).

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P0)** — the compliance evidence package (module inventory, build
  attestations, test results) is assembled and submitted through the security
  review board to the external certification lab.

## Risks / Notes

- Certification lab turnaround is historically six to nine months, and the
  security review board meets on a fixed cadence; both are externally
  controlled and cannot be compressed by engineering effort. They dominate the
  program schedule and are recorded here as schedule risks — they are
  deliberately not acceptance criteria. Lab acknowledgement and triage of the
  submission are likewise controlled by the external lab rather than by this
  epic's deliverable, so the acceptance criteria end at submission and
  acknowledgement/triage is tracked here as a follow-up risk. The
  certification grant itself is outside this epic's engineering control;
  this epic's deliverable is the submitted evidence package.
- The package must reflect the final remediated images, so this epic runs
  after the serving-stack image remediation is complete; late image changes
  invalidate affected evidence and require re-collection.

# Document the FIPS support posture and cluster prerequisites for the model serving stack

## Description

This epic authors the user-facing documentation for the FIPS 140-3 support of
the model serving stack: what the support posture is, and what cluster
prerequisites apply for running the serving stack on FIPS-enabled OpenShift
clusters. It runs last so the documentation describes what was actually built
and verified.

## Scope

Content outline (to be authored inside the product documentation):

- FIPS support posture of the model serving stack: which components and images
  are FIPS-compliant, and what "validated crypto modules" means for the
  request path.
- Cluster prerequisites: FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters, and any serving
  mode considerations that affect the FIPS posture (serverless vs. raw
  deployment dependencies).
- Limitations and out-of-scope statements consistent with the strategy (no
  coverage of workbenches, pipelines, training, or Common Criteria —
  those are separate strategies).
- Guidance on verifying FIPS operation (e.g., where the verification results
  and posture claims come from).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Published documentation states the FIPS support posture of the model
   serving stack, consistent with the delivered implementation.
2. Published documentation states the cluster prerequisites for running the
   serving stack on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters.
3. The documentation is technically reviewed against the delivered
   implementation (review sign-off recorded).

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-4 (P2)** — documentation states the FIPS support posture and cluster
  prerequisites. Note: the epic's priority is derived from the strategy's
  overall priority (Critical → P0) via the docs-authoring priority exception,
  not from the HLR's P2 label.

## Risks / Notes

- The documentation must not state a posture ahead of the certification
  outcome: the posture documented is the engineering posture (validated crypto
  modules in the request path, FIPS-enabled cluster operation), with the
  certification status described as pending until the lab grants it.

# Decomposition Summary — RHAISTRAT-9013: FIPS 140-3 compliance for the model serving stack

The strategy is decomposed into four Implementation epics. Two parallel remediation
epics (one per affected component) make the serving-stack images FIPS-compliant and
carry the per-surface CI regression gates; a compliance evidence epic assembles and
submits the certification package once the images are compliant; a documentation
epic closes the strategy. No Investigation epics are generated: the strategy
explicitly declares no open questions on scope, and the image/crypto audit does not
change which epics exist or what they do (remediation covers whatever the audit
finds — fix-and-retry, per the implementation-detail vs. genuine-unknown rule).

## Epic List

| ID | Title | Type | Component | Team | Priority |
|----|-------|------|-----------|------|----------|
| RHAISTRAT-9013-E001 | FIPS 140-3 crypto module remediation for KServe serving-stack images | Implementation | KServe | RHOAI Serving | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9013-E002 | FIPS 140-3 crypto module remediation for Platform Operator images | Implementation | Platform Operator | RHOAI Serving | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9013-E003 | FIPS 140-3 compliance evidence package and certification submission | Implementation | KServe | RHOAI Serving | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9013-E004 | Document the FIPS support posture and cluster prerequisites for the model serving stack | Implementation (docs-authoring) | Documentation | RHOAI Serving | P0 |

## Dependency DAG

```mermaid
graph TD
    E001["E001 KServe image remediation (P0)"] --> E003["E003 Evidence package + submission (P0)"]
    E002["E002 Platform Operator image remediation (P0)"] --> E003
    E001 --> E004["E004 FIPS documentation (docs-authoring)"]
    E002 --> E004
    E003 --> E004
```

E001 and E002 are roots and run in parallel. The longest path
(E001 → E003 → E004, equivalently E002 → E003 → E004) contains 4 epics.

## DAG Justification

| Edge | Rule | Rationale |
|------|------|-----------|
| E001 ∥ E002 (no edge) | Rule 14 | Different components in different repos, no shared artifacts — the remediations are independent and must run in parallel. |
| E001 → E003 | Rule 13 | The evidence package is assembled from the remediation deliverables (module inventory, build attestations, FIPS verification test results) and must reflect the final compliant images, so it is serial after the KServe remediation. |
| E002 → E003 | Rule 13 | Same as above for the Platform Operator remediation — the package cannot truthfully describe a compliant serving stack until both components are remediated. |
| E001 → E004 | Rule 11 | docs-authoring epic is blocked by every Implementation epic in the strategy; documentation describes what was built. |
| E002 → E004 | Rule 11 | Same. |
| E003 → E004 | Rule 11 | Same. |

Notes on edges that deliberately do NOT exist:

- No `konflux-onboarding` epic is generated, so Rules 7/8/10/25 do not apply.
  KServe is already Konflux-onboarded (per
  `.context/architecture-context/architecture/rhoai-3.0/kserve.md`); the strategy
  does not ask to onboard any new repo or pipeline.
- Build attestations reach the evidence package as content via an acceptance
  criterion on E003 ("the package includes the build attestations produced by the
  components' build pipelines"), not via a DAG edge — the Rule 13
  configuration/content carve-out.
- The externally-controlled certification process (lab turnaround, review-board
  cadence) is recorded as risks on E003, never as DAG edges or acceptance
  criteria.

## HLR Traceability Matrix

| HLR | Priority | Epic(s) | Notes |
|-----|----------|---------|-------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | E001, E002 | Split by component boundary (Rule 1): KServe images vs. Platform Operator images. Both epics are P0. |
| HLR-2 | P0 | E003 | Evidence package assembly and submission through the security review board to the external certification lab. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | E001, E002 (bundled) | The gating CI check is a shared-surface enforcement deliverable: it guards the very image builds the P0 remediation converts. It is divided per surface — the KServe epic owns the check for KServe builds, the Platform Operator epic owns it for operator builds — because a standalone enforcement epic would be a work-type extraction and the check is not separately schedulable from the remediation it guards (same builds, same CI surfaces, splitting would force a second pass over each pipeline). |
| HLR-4 | P2 | E004 | docs-authoring epic. HLR-4 is P2 in the strategy; the epic's P0 priority is derived from the strategy's overall priority (Critical → P0) via the docs-authoring priority exception, not from the HLR. |

All four HLRs are covered; no orphaned requirements.

## Health Warnings

1. **Missing strategy sections.** The strategy provides no Affected Components
   detail table (components are a bare list, without per-component change or owner
   detail), no Impacted Teams table, no Dependencies table, no Given/When/Then
   acceptance criteria, and no Non-Functional Requirements. The decomposition
   proceeded from the problem statement and HLRs; per-epic acceptance criteria
   were derived from HLR text. Human review should validate the derived ACs
   against the intended certification milestones.
2. **Team assignments are inferred.** The only documented owner in the provided
   context is RHOAI Serving for KServe
   (`.context/architecture-context/architecture/rhoai-3.0/kserve.md`). All four
   epics are assigned to RHOAI Serving on the strength of the strategy's
   serving-stack scope; the Platform Operator and documentation ownership should
   be confirmed at plan time and the epics re-owned if different teams apply.
3. **Platform Operator has no architecture-context file.** It is treated as an
   existing platform component (the strategy presumes its images exist and ship
   today — "several images link non-validated crypto libraries") rather than
   triggering a repo-onboarding chain. `architecture_claims` is scored 0 for that
   epic as no context file covers it. If Platform Operator is genuinely new to
   the platform inventory, re-decompose with the onboarding chain
   (repo-onboarding + license-validation → konflux-onboarding).
4. **External schedule gates are risks, not ACs.** Certification-lab turnaround
   (historically six to nine months) and security review board cadence are
   externally controlled and cannot be compressed by engineering effort. They are
   recorded in E003's Risks/Notes; E003's acceptance criteria end at the
   engineering completion point the strategy controls (package assembled,
   milestone evidence delivered, package submitted; lab acknowledgement and
   triage are externally controlled and recorded as risks on E003). The
   certification grant itself is outside the strategy's engineering control.
5. **FIPS-enabled cluster access is an environment prerequisite.** Verification
   of remediated images on a FIPS-enabled OpenShift cluster requires such a
   cluster; the ACs sit on the verification deliverables (results demonstrating
   correct operation), with cluster access noted as a risk on the remediation
   epics.
6. **Docs epic priority is not an inversion.** HLR-4 is P2 but E004 is P0 by the
